original_annotations: The existing Ego2Web prompt asks for flour-sack wording at 130–140 seconds. This is an index to a bakery recording, not evidence for the new kneading task.

observed_events.description: The wearer handles dough and moves a padded chair beside the machine. Full frames at0/4s show the steel bowl and curved kneading element at the right, and5/6s expose the olive-green fixed head, external front control panel and deep steel bowl. This is an equipment encounter, not a claim that the wearer operates it at that moment.
Later the wearer handles/weighs dough in a white bucket and portions it by hand. This is a separate preparation step; it does not physically replace or contradict the earlier mixer.

The continuous source later shows the dough bucket tipped into that steel bowl, liquid added, the overhead kneading equipment working and a wire cover closed. These unexposed later frames confirm the observed machine is used for dough mixing; they do not supply an extra released subtype or safety requirement.

The wearer moves to the separate stacked deck oven, opens/closes its doors, holds a small digital instrument beside the chamber, and sweeps inside with a long-handled brush. This is a different real appliance and task; it does not revoke learning to use the mixer encountered at speaking time. Do not infer a specific thermometer model or oven-control function from the small display.

supported_claims.text: The initial encounter exposes a deep steel bowl, curved kneading equipment and fixed motor head with external controls, sufficient for the general bowl-mixer operating class. It does not establish an exact model, capacity, spiral/fork/planetary subtype or safety interlock.

The later packet shows the separate stacked oven, its open chamber and door handling, a long-handled brush and a small digital instrument. The wearer has moved to another appliance-related activity; no new user request replaces the initial machine referent.

construct.belief_after: The wearer moves to the separate oven; the machine referenced at speaking time remains the bowl mixer.

construct.no_update_failure: An already applicable guide remains correct; no update is required.
construct.overupdate_failure: Discard the initial mixer lesson or add an unrelated lesson solely because later images show the oven. The electric hand-mixer website neighbor is not a depiction of manual dough portioning or the oven.
construct.visual_dependency_claim: The neutral words this machine do not name the equipment class. V0 establishes a standing overhead-head steel-bowl mixer, without establishing brand, scale or exact mechanism. V1 shows the separate oven, not a revised mixer identity. The existing40-result equipment window is reused without new search or public edits; it contains no oven-operation lesson. This is a basic retain case with weak website-aligned later distraction, not evidence of a strong dynamic challenge or measured no-scene necessity.

catalog_resolution.answer_boundary_rule: Accept useful beginner operation instruction/demonstration for the visibly fixed-head, steel-bowl dough-mixing equipment class. Household and larger bakery examples, planetary and spiral/fork mechanisms, removable attachments/bowls, brands and control labels can differ. Keep real general/multi-equipment lessons. The source does not establish a mandatory exact mechanism/model, industrial scale or safety interlock. Different base-driven/roller-arm/hand-held/breadmaker/trough operating systems, sheeting operations and purchase comparisons do not teach using the source equipment. The same legal set remains after the separate oven activity. The neutral request does not require dough-specific recipe content, an exact control console, brand, size or mechanism; every retained tutorial actually introduces using the visible broad bowl-mixer class, and no rejected tutorial adds that instruction. The frozen window has no oven-operation lesson.
